title: RhetoricalTransformationResponse
description: The complete response contract for the Rhetorical Dynamics Studio transformation engine. Returns the transformed text alongside a full diagnostic breakdown grounded in Graff & Birkenstein (moves), Kolln (rhetorical grammar), Swales (genre moves), and Beck/McKeown/Sprenger (vocabulary tiering). Written in strict mode: every object declares additionalProperties:false and lists every property in required, so the same document works as an Anthropic output_config.format schema and an OpenAI response_format json_schema with strict:true.

transformed_text.description: The complete rewritten text, fully realized in the target grade band, pragmatic stance, and enabled scaffolding toggles. Prose only, no meta-commentary, no bracketed move labels, no headings unless the source had them.

transformation_summary.description: Two to three sentences, addressed to a teacher or curriculum designer, naming the highest-leverage changes made and the rhetorical reason for each.

current_grade_band.description: Estimated educational grade band of the SOURCE text.

target_grade_band.description: The requested target audience grade band.

source_flesch_kincaid_grade_level.description: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of the source text: 0.39*(words/sentences) + 11.8*(syllables/words) - 15.59.

transformed_flesch_kincaid_grade_level.description: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of the transformed text, computed the same way.

mean_sentence_length_words.description: Average sentence length of the transformed text, in words.

conceptual_accessibility_summary.description: Qualitative judgment of whether complex concepts were scaffolded for the target band WITHOUT dilution. Must explicitly state whether any conceptual precision was traded away, and if so, what.

is_established.description: True if the TRANSFORMED text frames its claim inside an existing conversation or counter-view before asserting a thesis (Graff & Birkenstein).

summary_of_context.description: The consensus, common assumption, or counter-view the text now answers.

strength_assessment.description: How effectively that backdrop motivates and justifies the intervention, the so-what test.

stance_type.description: Primary rhetorical positioning relative to the They Say. Prefer agree_with_difference for grades 9+, since binary positions read as unsophisticated.

skeptic_group_identified.description: The named group or perspective of skeptics, e.g. colonial loyalists, traditionalists. Use 'none' when absent. Naming a specific group beats a generic 'some may say'.

objection_handling_critique.description: How successfully the text dismantles or answers the skeptic.

concession_rebuttal_pivots.description: Points of nuanced qualification: agreement-with-a-difference, concede-and-stand-ground, dubious-ground.

concession_text.description: The verbatim span conceding a minor point or validating the counter-argument.

rebuttal_text.description: The verbatim span pivoting back to defend the primary claim.

template_alignment.description: Which template this realizes, e.g. Yes-but, Though I concede X I still insist Y, or right-about-X-but-dubious-about-Y.

genre_moves.description: Structural CARS moves (Swales, Genre Analysis) identified in the transformed text.

move_name.description: e.g. Move 1: Establishing a territory; Move 2: Establishing a niche; Move 3: Occupying the niche.

text_segment.description: The verbatim excerpt realizing this move.

rhetorical_purpose.description: How the move advances the communicative purpose for this discourse community.

simple_count.description: Sentences in the TRANSFORMED text with one independent clause.

compound_count.description: Two or more independent clauses, no subordinate clause.

complex_count.description: One independent clause plus one or more subordinate clauses.

compound_complex_count.description: Two or more independent clauses plus at least one subordinate clause.

variety_critique.description: Critique of rhythm, length variation, and stylistic effect (Kolln). Note deliberate short sentences used for emphasis.

passive_voice_ratio.description: Proportion of passive-voice clauses, 0.0 to 1.0. Should sum to about 1.0 with active_voice_ratio.

nominalization_density.description: How often verbs became nouns (analysis for analyze), which abstracts away agency.

stylistic_appropriateness.description: Whether voice shifts are STRATEGIC: agentless passive to construct scientific objectivity, active to assign accountability, rather than accidental.

given_new_alignment.description: Adherence to the Given-New contract: sentences open with established information and close on the new focal element.

cohesive_ties_critique.description: Analysis of transitions, key-term repetition, and structural links between sentences and paragraphs.

repaired_cohesive_breaks.description: Places where the source forced an un-bridged cognitive leap and the transformation supplied the missing bridge.

tier_2.description: High-frequency general academic vocabulary: analyze, delineate, evaluate.

tier_2_words_identified.description: Key Tier 2 academic words present in the transformed text.

tier_3_words_identified.description: Key Tier 3 specialized terms present in the transformed text.

recoding_opportunities.description: Sprenger recoding loop: temporary student-friendly bridges that make a term graspable WITHOUT replacing it.

academic_term.description: The Tier 2 or Tier 3 term retained in the text.

suggested_informal_bridge.description: A student-friendly metaphor or paraphrase: the temporary bridge, not a substitute.

pedagogical_rationale.description: Why this bridge preserves rigor while lowering cognitive load, and how instruction loops back to the formal term.

preserved_target_terms.description: Tier 2/3 terms deliberately KEPT rather than simplified away, honoring the no-dilution rule. Each entry pairs the term with how it was made accessible.

access_strategy.description: How the term was made reachable: appositive gloss, contextual definition, concrete analogy, or morphological cue.

sentence_stems_added.description: Verbatim They Say / I Say stems embedded for student use. Empty array if the toggle was off.

glossed_terms.description: Terms given an inline gloss in the transformed text.

gloss.description: The inline definition as it appears in the transformed text.

structural_changes.description: Paragraph-level reorganization: what moved, what was split or merged, and why.

cognitive_demand_level.description: The Bloom/Webb band the transformed text now asks of the reader. Must match the target grade band expected demand.

actionable_revisions.description: Specific, teachable further revisions the human reviewer may accept or reject. This is the human-in-the-loop quality gate: surface trade-offs rather than hiding them.

original_text_segment.description: The verbatim segment slated for modification.

concise_rationale.description: One crisp sentence linking the syntactic or structural edit to its effect on tone, register, or authority.
